name: GALI-S66+
title: GALI-S66+: 50 Ω InGaP HBT Darlington MMIC gain block, DC to 3 GHz, SOT-89
summary: A broadband, high-dynamic-range gain block built as an InGaP HBT Darlington pair, matched to 50 Ω at both ports, in a four-lead SOT-89 plastic case (DF782) whose exposed metal tab is ground. It gives about 21.6 dB of gain at 100 MHz falling to 16.4 dB at 3 GHz, with a 2.4 dB noise figure and +3.3 dBm output at 1 dB compression at 2 GHz. Bias goes in through the output lead: it runs at 16 mA with about 3.5 V across it, fed from a higher supply through a series resistor and, optionally, an RF choke; both RF ports need DC-blocking capacitors. Its Darlington is protected against transients, so it withstands ESD and supply turn-on surges.

circuits.title: Recommended application circuit
circuits.description: The amplifier as a 50 Ω gain stage. C1 and C2 keep DC out of the signal ports. Supply current comes from Vcc through R1, which sets the 16 mA bias current, and through the optional choke L1 to pin 3, which sits at the device voltage Vd. C3 bypasses the supply end of R1 to ground. Pick R1 from the bias resistor table for the supply in use. Pins 2 and 4 go to ground.

operation.text: An InGaP HBT Darlington pair with transient protection, built to withstand ESD and supply switch-on surges. Performance repeats closely from lot to lot.
Cellular and PCS equipment, and communication receivers and transmitters.

The recommended operating current is 16 mA, at which the device drops +3.0 to +4.0 V (3.5 V typ). A resistor from a higher supply sets the current, with values listed for 7 to 20 V supplies. The device voltage falls about 2.1 mV per °C at 16 mA and rises about 3.7 mV per mA of extra current. Current must stay under 50 mA.
The device itself works down to DC; the lowest usable frequency in a circuit is set by the DC-blocking capacitors at input and output.

The package has an exposed metal bottom for heat dissipation and low thermal resistance; junction-to-ground-lead resistance is 64 °C/W. Ground pins 2 and 4 through vias close to the leads, following layout PL-019, to keep ground inductance low. The part tolerates aqueous washing.

MSL1 is qualified on 45 units: visual check at 40x, room-temperature electrical test and acoustic microscope (SAM) scan; then a 24 h bake at 125 °C, 168 h soak at 85 °C and 85 %RH, and three reflows peaking at 260 °C; then the visual, electrical and SAM checks again, with delamination allowed to grow by under 10%.
